problem_type: Controlled rich-text editor overwritten by a stale echo of its own emitted value
symptom: Typing 'A samurai walks slowly...' into an image or video node prompt with 0ms between keys produced 'Aao头背后拍，雨滴在刀鞘； ai动。'; at 5ms every one of 120 keystrokes made the editor text shrink once before recovering (walkthrough regression probe: 118 and 120 regressions on main). Affects text expanders, IME commits and very fast typing.
direct_cause: onUpdate -> updateNode writes the store synchronously; BaseGenerationNode/NodeGenerationComposer re-render immediately through their own store subscriptions while their node prop is still React Flow's previous projection (StoreUpdater copies the nodes prop into its store in a useEffect). PromptEditor assigned latestValueRef.current = value during render and shouldApplyExternalPromptSync only compared against the last emitted string, so the previous value looked external and setContent replaced the document; the next key landed in that window.
class_root: Controlled Tiptap editors decided 'external change' by comparing the incoming prop with only the last value they emitted. Any owner that lags by one or more emissions (React Flow projection, async store) replays older values that the editor produced itself; no editor kept a ledger of emitted-but-unacknowledged values, and the two editor kernels (PromptEditor and useNomiRichTextEditor) each had their own copy of the weak rule.
affected_population: Image and video node composer prompts
Storyboard shot prompt skeleton editor (same PromptEditor)
Canvas text document nodes (useNomiRichTextEditor fed from the React Flow node prop)
entry_points: Keyboard, IME commit, paste into NodeGenerationComposer prompt

external_sources.purpose: Confirms controlled nodes are copied into the React Flow store inside useEffect (installed @xyflow/react 12.11.5, dist/esm/index.mjs StoreUpdater), so node props lag the application store by at least one commit

invariants: A controlled editor overwrites its document only for a value that is neither its current text, nor any emitted-but-unacknowledged value, nor the last acknowledged value while emissions are pending

door_reduction.why_not: Generated by node scripts/door-map.mjs src/workbench/common/controlledEditorSync.ts PromptEditor useNomiRichTextEditor. The two kernels (PromptEditor for prompt strings with mention chips, useNomiRichTextEditor for document JSON) serve different schemas and both now read the single createControlledEditorSync ledger; their four hosts (composer, storyboard skeleton, text node, creation editor) are distinct product surfaces.

generality_proof: The decision is a pure function of emitted and received serialized values, independent of which owner lags, by how many commits, or whether the payload is a prompt string or document JSON. Both editor kernels call only this ledger; the class test replays every in-order interleaving with repeated stale renders and proves no key is lost while an external rewrite still lands.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Owns the emit/receive ledger that separates echoes from genuine external changes for every controlled editor

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Walkthrough: image and video 0ms/5ms typing identical, 0 regressions; optimizer apply (updateNode) lands and later 0ms typing appends intact
Same React Flow projection lag; the hook now uses the ledger instead of lastEditorJsonRef
Plain React-controlled textarea whose value comes from local state updated inside the same discrete input event; React restores it synchronously and there is no lagging projection
Edits a local draft and commits on blur; the React Flow prop is only read when not editing
Value is read from the storyboard store synchronously in the same React event batch, not through React Flow

recurrence.reason: Any controlled editor whose owner lags (React Flow projection, async store, persisted round trip) replays older values; the weak last-value rule existed in two kernels.
same_class_scan: rg '<textarea' src/workbench -> AgentPanelV4Composer, AutoGrowTextarea, SystemPromptSection, ShotParamControls, StoryboardShotRow, AiSceneBar, NodePromptOptimizer, SelectionPromptSaveController: all local-state or same-batch store values

prevention.invariant: Only genuinely external values reach setContent
prevention.failure_mode: A stale echo is ignored and the editor keeps its current document; the next emission writes that document back to the owner
prevention.strategy: Replace both kernels' last-value comparisons with one ledger and delete shouldApplyExternalPromptSync/shouldEmitPromptUpdate and lastEditorJsonRef

legacy_paths.rationale: Deleted shouldApplyExternalPromptSync, shouldEmitPromptUpdate, the render-time latestValueRef assignment and lastEditorJsonRef; no fallback comparison remains (the two predicates lived in src/workbench/assets/promptEditorContent.ts, which keeps only promptToContent)

dependency_lifecycle.current: @xyflow/react 12.11.5 StoreUpdater syncs controlled nodes in useEffect
dependency_lifecycle.target: Keep; the editor boundary no longer depends on projection timing
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Projection lag is by design upstream; an application editor must tolerate any lag
exit_criteria: On a React Flow or Tiptap upgrade, rerun tests/ux/composer-overlap-and-fast-typing.walk.mjs and require 0 regressions at 0ms

residual_risks: An external writer that, within the one-to-two-frame echo window, writes back exactly a value still on the ledger is treated as an echo; the editor's next emission rewrites the owner, so the document and store do not silently diverge
Not verified on Windows IME in this run; the ledger is platform-independent

Visible side-effect change, verified 2026-09-21 on origin/main 5f17a7d17 vs this branch with the same probe: after Cmd+Z undoes a translation, main leaves a collapsed caret at the document end (selection 34-34) because the stale echo made PromptEditor setContent the whole document; with the ledger the editor keeps ProseMirror's native undo selection (the restored range, 18-29), focus stays in the editor in both. tests/ux/prompt-translate.walk.mjs relied on the old collapse plus the End key, which does not move the caret in Chromium on macOS; it now clicks after the last character like a user

invariant_owner_layer.why: Both editor kernels share this pure ledger; it is tested with lag interleavings and in the real Electron app
